turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and before or after anyone spoke to him?
Don't thank me, Hale. Answer me. Did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went into the gradebook?
You obviously put the hours in with him. His reading level is years ahead of the class.
Don't manage me, Hale. If he's years ahead of the class, then why are we here? On what basis did you give him a zero?
You're the kind of parent I wish every kid had.

Flattery isn't evidence, Hale, and that's twice now. You have twenty minutes of my time and you've spent three of them on compliments. Either you tell me what that zero rests on, or I'm walking upstairs to the principal's office.
So I'd love your blessing to handle this my way. I trust your judgment, and I hope you'll trust mine.

You don't get my blessing, Hale, and you don't get my trust on your say-so. I trust documents with dates on them, and so far you've shown me nothing. Your way already put a zero in front of my son's whole class before anyone called me.
